k: A statue of the first Hierophant, arms raised to the sun. Someone has chalked a mustache on him. It is a very good mustache.
src: 'A statue of the first Hierophant, arms raised to the sun. Someone has chalked a mustache on him. It is a very good mustache.'

k: A Dawnguard cot, the blanket squared to regulation. Pinned above it: a child's drawing of a knight with a very large sword, signed TO DAD.
src: 'A Dawnguard cot, the blanket squared to regulation. Pinned above it: a child\'s drawing of a knight with a very large sword, signed TO DAD.'

k: The cradle of the Great Lamp of Aurenne. The glass is cracked from rim to base. It was the brightest light in the world for nine hundred years.
src: 'The cradle of the Great Lamp of Aurenne. The glass is cracked from rim to base. It was the brightest light in the world for nine hundred years.'

k: Well
src: 'Well'

k: Garden
src: 'Garden'

k: The village Hearthstone. Cold, for the first time in anyone's memory. Someone has left a bunch of dried sea-lavender on it.
src: 'The village Hearthstone. Cold, for the first time in anyone\'s memory. Someone has left a bunch of dried sea-lavender on it.'

k: Tobias's shack. A note pinned under a stone in his square capitals: BACK SOON. DON'T TOUCH THE NETS. The nets are still here. Nobody touched them.
src: 'Tobias\'s shack. A note pinned under a stone in his square capitals: BACK SOON. DON\'T TOUCH THE NETS. The nets are still here. Nobody touched them.'

k: Nana Brisa's house. Through the window, jars of herbs labeled in tiny exact handwriting. One just says: DO NOT. LET WREN. TOUCH.
src: 'Nana Brisa\'s house. Through the window, jars of herbs labeled in tiny exact handwriting. One just says: DO NOT. LET WREN. TOUCH.'

k: Two plates. Two cups. A year of ash on both.
src: 'Two plates. Two cups. A year of ash on both.'

k: Your bed. Unmade, obviously. Some things survive the end of the world.
src: 'Your bed. Unmade, obviously. Some things survive the end of the world.'

k: Your father's books. Sea charts, star charts, and the pirate-queen novel with the last chapter torn out. Tucked in its place, a folded paper in your mother's hand: "She ends up happy. Don't tell Wren, she'll want to read it herself."
src: 'Your father\'s books. Sea charts, star charts, and the pirate-queen novel with the last chapter torn out. Tucked in its place, a folded paper in your mother\'s hand: "She ends up happy. Don\'t tell Wren, she\'ll want to read it herself."'

k: Your own books, salt-stiff. The Sunward Atlas is not among them. You took it with you. You remember choosing it over a sweater.
src: 'Your own books, salt-stiff. The Sunward Atlas is not among them. You took it with you. You remember choosing it over a sweater.'

k: The great lamp of Lanternfall, dark. Inside the brass, where the Dawnstone used to sleep, nothing at all. It is only a lamp now.
src: 'The great lamp of Lanternfall, dark. Inside the brass, where the Dawnstone used to sleep, nothing at all. It is only a lamp now.'

k: Lantern log
src: 'Lantern log'

k: Wreck
src: 'Wreck'

k: A Choir supply barge, sunk with its cargo: thousands of candles, still in their wrappers. Every one unlit.
src: 'A Choir supply barge, sunk with its cargo: thousands of candles, still in their wrappers. Every one unlit.'

k: An old Aurenne galleon, two hundred years down. The figurehead is a woman holding a lantern. Someone, long ago, gave her a face like a mother's.
src: 'An old Aurenne galleon, two hundred years down. The figurehead is a woman holding a lantern. Someone, long ago, gave her a face like a mother\'s.'

k: A smuggler's sloop. In the hold, crates stamped PROPERTY OF C. ASHE — DO NOT OPEN. Corvin pretends not to see them.
src: 'A smuggler\'s sloop. In the hold, crates stamped PROPERTY OF C. ASHE — DO NOT OPEN. Corvin pretends not to see them.'

k: A cot, made with hospital corners. A child's drawing is tucked under the pillow: a big woman in a hood, and the words MOTHER OSK MAKES IT STOP HURTING.
src: 'A cot, made with hospital corners. A child\'s drawing is tucked under the pillow: a big woman in a hood, and the words MOTHER OSK MAKES IT STOP HURTING.'

k: A cot, made with hospital corners. On the blanket, a single dried flower, placed very carefully.
src: 'A cot, made with hospital corners. On the blanket, a single dried flower, placed very carefully.'

k: Vigil stone
src: 'Vigil stone'

k: A cairn of gray stones. On the largest, chiseled by someone who was not a mason: SIR ALDOUS VENN. HE STOOD BETWEEN.
src: 'A cairn of gray stones. On the largest, chiseled by someone who was not a mason: SIR ALDOUS VENN. HE STOOD BETWEEN.'

k: A stone knight, sword point-down, head bowed. The plinth reads: DAME ORSOLA OF THE WESTMARCH. SHE WAS AFRAID OF HORSES.
src: 'A stone knight, sword point-down, head bowed. The plinth reads: DAME ORSOLA OF THE WESTMARCH. SHE WAS AFRAID OF HORSES.'

k: A stone knight with a cracked shield. The plinth reads: SIR TEODOR BRAND. HE WEPT AT EVERY KNIGHTING, INCLUDING HIS OWN.
src: 'A stone knight with a cracked shield. The plinth reads: SIR TEODOR BRAND. HE WEPT AT EVERY KNIGHTING, INCLUDING HIS OWN.'

k: A stone knight, very young, very serious. The plinth reads: SIR ALDOUS VENN, AGE NINETEEN. Somebody has scratched underneath, much later: STILL AN IDIOT. — G.T.
src: 'A stone knight, very young, very serious. The plinth reads: SIR ALDOUS VENN, AGE NINETEEN. Somebody has scratched underneath, much later: STILL AN IDIOT. — G.T.'

k: The Rook Queen's nest: a ring of buttons, spoons, bottle caps, a brass doorknob, three wedding rings and, right in the middle, a child-sized empty space shaped like a knife.
src: 'The Rook Queen\'s nest: a ring of buttons, spoons, bottle caps, a brass doorknob, three wedding rings and, right in the middle, a child-sized empty space shaped like a knife.'

k: A kite with a lopsided sun painted on it, tangled in the junk. A name on the spar in crayon: TILLY. PROPERTY OF. KEEP OFF.
src: 'A kite with a lopsided sun painted on it, tangled in the junk. A name on the spar in crayon: TILLY. PROPERTY OF. KEEP OFF.'

k: Hal's cabin
src: 'Hal\'s cabin'

k: The Kingfisher's mainmast, snapped. Her colors still fly from the stump: Dawnguard blue, with a kingfisher stitched over the sunburst by someone who could not sew.
src: 'The Kingfisher\'s mainmast, snapped. Her colors still fly from the stump: Dawnguard blue, with a kingfisher stitched over the sunburst by someone who could not sew.'

k: A bow gun, still loaded. The gunner's gloves are on the breech, laid down neatly side by side, as if he meant to come back for them.
src: 'A bow gun, still loaded. The gunner\'s gloves are on the breech, laid down neatly side by side, as if he meant to come back for them.'

k: A small bed with a patchwork quilt. Every patch is a different shade of yellow.
src: 'A small bed with a patchwork quilt. Every patch is a different shade of yellow.'

k: A shelf of wooden animals: a gull, a cat, a lopsided horse. Carved by a twelve-year-old, badly, with enormous care.
src: 'A shelf of wooden animals: a gull, a cat, a lopsided horse. Carved by a twelve-year-old, badly, with enormous care.'

k: Telescope
src: 'Telescope'

k: A star chart, inked on sailcloth. Half the stars are crossed out. Beside the gaps, in tiny writing: "fell?" "fell." "FELL. Bother."
src: 'A star chart, inked on sailcloth. Half the stars are crossed out. Beside the gaps, in tiny writing: "fell?" "fell." "FELL. Bother."'

k: A copy of The Sunward Atlas, annotated in red ink by its own author. The margins are fuller than the pages.
src: 'A copy of The Sunward Atlas, annotated in red ink by its own author. The margins are fuller than the pages.'

k: A shelf of books about the sun. Every one ends with the same chapter title: "And Then It Rose Again."
src: 'A shelf of books about the sun. Every one ends with the same chapter title: "And Then It Rose Again."'

k: The door is painted shut. Everything here is.
src: 'The door is painted shut. Everything here is.'

k: Two plates. Two cups. A third chair, pushed in, that nobody has sat in for seven years.
src: 'Two plates. Two cups. A third chair, pushed in, that nobody has sat in for seven years.'

k: Your father's books. Sea charts. Star charts. A novel about a pirate queen with the last chapter torn out.
src: 'Your father\'s books. Sea charts. Star charts. A novel about a pirate queen with the last chapter torn out.'

k: A statue of the Hierophant as a young man, arms open. The plinth reads: HE WHO KEPT THE LIGHT. Someone has scratched underneath: AND KEPT IT. AND KEPT IT.
src: 'A statue of the Hierophant as a young man, arms open. The plinth reads: HE WHO KEPT THE LIGHT. Someone has scratched underneath: AND KEPT IT. AND KEPT IT.'

k: A statue of a girl of ten holding a book against her chest. The plinth has no name on it. It doesn't need one.
src: 'A statue of a girl of ten holding a book against her chest. The plinth has no name on it. It doesn\'t need one.'

k: Seven sockets are set into the paving before the arch, each shaped like a jagged piece of something round.
src: 'Seven sockets are set into the paving before the arch, each shaped like a jagged piece of something round.'

k: A belfry bell, toppled and cracked. Its clapper has been removed and laid neatly beside it, like a sleeping child.
src: 'A belfry bell, toppled and cracked. Its clapper has been removed and laid neatly beside it, like a sleeping child.'

k: A Vesper soldier's helmet, half-buried in ash. Inside, a folded note: "Mira — if the sun really stops, I'll be home for supper forever. Save me a seat." The ink has faded to violet.
src: 'A Vesper soldier\'s helmet, half-buried in ash. Inside, a folded note: "Mira — if the sun really stops, I\'ll be home for supper forever. Save me a seat." The ink has faded to violet.'

k: A small stone at the foot of the arch. Two names, carved by an unpracticed hand: LYSA LORNE. CASSIAN LORNE. Underneath, smaller: "Now they both know where the sun goes."
src: 'A small stone at the foot of the arch. Two names, carved by an unpracticed hand: LYSA LORNE. CASSIAN LORNE. Underneath, smaller: "Now they both know where the sun goes."'

k: Beyond the arch there is only a bright, ordinary morning, and a long way down.
src: 'Beyond the arch there is only a bright, ordinary morning, and a long way down.'

k: Halcyon's staying tied off till this is done, sparrow. No coming back — you said it yourself.
src: 'Halcyon\'s staying tied off till this is done, sparrow. No coming back — you said it yourself.'

k: Where Evernoon stood there is only the shard, and the wall, and a quiet morning under the new sun. The golden afternoon is gone. Nobody misses it as much as they thought they would.
src: 'Where Evernoon stood there is only the shard, and the wall, and a quiet morning under the new sun. The golden afternoon is gone. Nobody misses it as much as they thought they would.'

k: The dancer smiles at you. Somewhere, faintly, a clock is ticking.
src: 'The dancer smiles at you. Somewhere, faintly, a clock is ticking.'

k: Lemonade! Fresh lemonade! And... swords, apparently. I don't remember stocking swords. I don't remember stocking anything.
src: 'Lemonade! Fresh lemonade! And... swords, apparently. I don\'t remember stocking swords. I don\'t remember stocking anything.'

k: Funny. Same lemon. I've been squeezing the same lemon all afternoon.
src: 'Funny. Same lemon. I\'ve been squeezing the same lemon all afternoon.'

k: Lovely afternoon. Lovely.
src: 'Lovely afternoon. Lovely.'

k: I keep meaning to go home for supper. Mira will have the soup on.
src: 'I keep meaning to go home for supper. Mira will have the soup on.'

k: Lovely afternoon.
src: 'Lovely afternoon.'

k: Two sweethearts lean toward each other. They have been leaning toward each other for forty years.
src: 'Two sweethearts lean toward each other. They have been leaning toward each other for forty years.'

k: Just KISS already.
src: 'Just KISS already.'

k: Let them have it, kid. Some moments are worth taking slow.
src: 'Let them have it, kid. Some moments are worth taking slow.'

k: Forty years is not slow, Corvin. Forty years is a medical condition.
src: 'Forty years is not slow, Corvin. Forty years is a medical condition.'

k: Three balls in the air above the juggler's hands. They never come down. They never go up, either.
src: 'Three balls in the air above the juggler\'s hands. They never come down. They never go up, either.'
